sentences.title: Australia (continent)
sentences.sentence_text: The continent of Australia, sometimes known in technical contexts as Sahul, Australia-New Guinea, Australinea, or Meganesia to distinguish it from the country of Australia, is located within the Southern and Eastern hemispheres, near the Maritime Southeast Asia.

sentences.title: Australia (continent)
sentences.sentence_text: The continent includes mainland Australia, Tasmania, the island of New Guinea, the Aru Islands, the Ashmore and Cartier Islands, most of the Coral Sea Islands, and some other nearby islands.

sentences.title: Australia (continent)
sentences.sentence_text: Situated in the geographical region of Oceania, more specifically in the subregion of Australasia, Australia is the smallest of the seven traditional continents.

sentences.title: Continent
sentences.sentence_text: A continent is any of several large terrestrial geographical regions.

sentences.title: Continent
sentences.sentence_text: Continents are generally identified by convention rather than any strict criteria.

sentences.title: Continent
sentences.sentence_text: A continent could be a single large landmass, a landmass and nearby islands either on or beyond its continental shelf, or a part of a larger landmass, as in the case of Asia and Europe within Eurasia.

sentences.title: Continent
sentences.sentence_text: Due to these varying definitions, the number of continents varies, up to seven or as few as four.

sentences.title: Continent
sentences.sentence_text: Most English-speaking countries recognize seven continents.

sentences.title: Continent
sentences.sentence_text: In order from largest to smallest in area, these seven are Asia, Africa, North America, South America, Antarctica, Europe, and Australia.

sentences.title: Continent
sentences.sentence_text: Different variations with fewer continents merge some of these regions; examples of this are merging Asia and Europe into Eurasia, North America and South America into the Americas, and Africa, Asia, and Europe into Afro-Eurasia.

sentences.title: Australia
sentences.sentence_text: Australia, officially the Commonwealth of Australia, is a country comprising the mainland of the Australian continent, the island of Tasmania and numerous smaller islands.

sentences.title: Australia
sentences.sentence_text: It has a total area of 7,688,287 km2 (2,968,464 sq mi), making it the sixth-largest country in the world and the largest in Oceania.

sentences.title: Australia
sentences.sentence_text: Australia is the world's flattest and driest inhabited continent.

sentences.title: Australia
sentences.sentence_text: It is a megadiverse country, and its size gives it a wide variety of landscapes and climates including deserts in the interior and tropical rainforests along the coast.

sentences.title: Australian Labor Party
sentences.sentence_text: The Australian Labor Party (ALP), also known simply as Labor, is the major social democratic and centre-left political party in Australia.

sentences.title: Australian Labor Party
sentences.sentence_text: Founded in 1891, it is the oldest political party in Australia and one of two major parties in Australian politics, its main rival being the Liberal Party of Australia.

sentences.title: Country music
sentences.sentence_text: Country music, also known as country and western or simply country, is a music genre known for its ballads and dance tunes, identifiable by both traditional lyrics and harmonies accompanied by banjos, mandolins, fiddles, harmonicas, and many types of guitar; either acoustic, electric, steel, or resonator guitars.

sentences.title: Country music
sentences.sentence_text: Once called hillbilly music, the term country music was popularized in the 1940s to give it a correct term.

sentences.title: Australians
sentences.sentence_text: Australians, colloquially known as Aussies, are the citizens, nationals and individuals associated with the country of Australia.

sentences.title: Australians
sentences.sentence_text: This connection may be residential, legal, historical or ethno-cultural.

sentences.title: Australians
sentences.sentence_text: For most Australians, several of these connections exist and are collectively the source of their being Australian.

sentences.title: Australians
sentences.sentence_text: Australian law does not provide for any racial or ethnic component of nationality, instead relying on citizenship to define being an 'Australian'.

sentences.title: Australians
sentences.sentence_text: Since the postwar period, Australia has pursued an official policy of multiculturalism and has the world's eighth-largest immigrant population, with immigrants accounting for 30 percent of the population in 2019.

sentences.title: Australian Open
sentences.sentence_text: The Australian Open is a tennis tournament organised by Tennis Australia annually at Melbourne Park in Melbourne, Victoria, Australia.

sentences.title: Australian Open
sentences.sentence_text: It is the first of the four major tennis tournaments every year, held before the French Open, Wimbledon and the US Open.

sentences.title: Australia (disambiguation)
sentences.sentence_text: Australia is a country in the Southern Hemisphere.

sentences.title: Australia Zoo
sentences.sentence_text: The Australia Zoo, previously known as the Beerwah Reptile and Fauna Park and the Queensland Reptile and Fauna Park, is a zoo located in Beerwah, a suburb of the Sunshine Coast region in Queensland, Australia.

sentences.title: Australia Zoo
sentences.sentence_text: Encompassing over 750 acres of bushland, 110 of which are open to the public, the zoo hosts over 1,200 animals.

sentences.title: Australia Zoo
sentences.sentence_text: It was opened on 3 June 1970 by Bob and Lyn Irwin, and is a regional member of the Zoo and Aquarium Association (ZAA).

sentences.title: Kerala
sentences.sentence_text: Kerala is a state of India on the Malabar Coast.

sentences.title: Kerala
sentences.sentence_text: It was formed on 1 November 1956 under the States Reorganisation Act, which unified the country's Malayalam-speaking regions into a single state.

sentences.title: Kerala
sentences.sentence_text: Covering 38,863 km2 (15,005 sq mi), it is bordered by Karnataka to the north and northeast, Tamil Nadu to the east and south, and the Laccadive Sea to the west.

sentences.title: Kerala
sentences.sentence_text: With 33 million inhabitants according to the 2011 census, Kerala is the 13th-most populous state in India.

sentences.title: Kerala
sentences.sentence_text: It is divided into 14 districts, with Thiruvananthapuram as the capital.

sentences.title: Kerala
sentences.sentence_text: Malayalam is the most widely spoken language and, along with English, serves as an official language of the state.

sentences.title: Global cancer statistics
sentences.sentence_text: The global burden of cancer continues to increase largely because of the aging and growth of the world population alongside an increasing adoption of cancer-causing behaviors, particularly smoking, in economically developing countries.

sentences.title: Global cancer statistics
sentences.sentence_text: Based on the GLOBOCAN 2008 estimates, about 12.7 million cancer cases and 7.6 million cancer deaths are estimated to have occurred in 2008; of these, 56% of the cases and 64% of the deaths occurred in the economically developing world.

sentences.title: Global cancer statistics
sentences.sentence_text: Breast cancer is the most frequently diagnosed cancer and the leading cause of cancer death among females, accounting for 23% of the total cancer cases and 14% of the cancer deaths.

sentences.title: Global cancer statistics
sentences.sentence_text: Lung cancer is the leading cancer site in males, comprising 17% of the total new cancer cases and 23% of the total cancer deaths.

sentences.title: Global cancer statistics
sentences.sentence_text: Breast cancer is now also the leading cause of cancer death among females in economically developing countries, a shift from the previous decade during which the most common cause of cancer death was cervical cancer.

sentences.title: Global cancer statistics
sentences.sentence_text: Further, the mortality burden for lung cancer among females in developing countries is as high as the burden for cervical cancer, with each accounting for 11% of the total female cancer deaths.

sentences.title: Global cancer statistics
sentences.sentence_text: Although overall cancer incidence rates in the developing world are half those seen in the developed world in both sexes, the overall cancer mortality rates are generally similar.

sentences.title: Global cancer statistics
sentences.sentence_text: Cancer survival tends to be poorer in developing countries, most likely because of a combination of a late stage at diagnosis and limited access to timely and standard treatment.

sentences.title: Global cancer statistics
sentences.sentence_text: A substantial proportion of the worldwide burden of cancer could be prevented through the application of existing cancer control knowledge and by implementing programs for tobacco control, vaccination (for liver and cervical cancers), and early detection and treatment, as well as public health campaigns promoting physical activity and a healthier dietary intake.

sentences.title: Global cancer statistics
sentences.sentence_text: Clinicians, public health professionals, and policy makers can play an active role in accelerating the application of such interventions globally.

sentences.title: Estimating the world cancer burden: Globocan 2000
sentences.sentence_text: Describing the distribution of disease between different populations and over time has been a highly successful way of devising hypotheses about causation and for quantifying the potential for preventive activities.1 Statistical data are also essential components of disease surveillance programs.

sentences.title: Estimating the world cancer burden: Globocan 2000
sentences.sentence_text: These play a critical role in the development and implementation of health policy, through identification of health problems, decisions on priorities for preventive and curative programs and evaluation of outcomes of programs of prevention, early detection/screening and treatment in relation to resource inputs.

sentences.title: Estimating the world cancer burden: Globocan 2000
sentences.sentence_text: Over the last 12 years, a series of estimates of the global burden of cancer have been published in the International Journal of Cancer.2-6 The methods have evolved and been refined, but basically they rely upon the best available data on cancer incidence and/or mortality at country level to build up the global picture.

sentences.title: Estimating the world cancer burden: Globocan 2000
sentences.sentence_text: The results are more or less accurate for different countries, depending on the extent and accuracy of locally available data.

sentences.title: Estimating the world cancer burden: Globocan 2000
sentences.sentence_text: This "data-based" approach is rather different from the modeling method used in other estimates.7-10 Essentially, these use sets of regression models, which predict cause-specific mortality rates of different populations from the corresponding all-cause mortality.11 The constants of the regression equations derive from datasets with different overall mortality rates (often including historic data from western countries).

sentences.title: Estimating the world cancer burden: Globocan 2000
sentences.sentence_text: Cancer deaths are then subdivided into the different cancer types, according to the best available information on relative frequencies.

sentences.title: Estimating the world cancer burden: Globocan 2000
sentences.sentence_text: GLOBOCAN 2000 updates the previously published data-based global estimates of incidence, mortality and prevalence to the year 2000.12 The data sources that have been used to build up the global estimates are as follows.

sentences.title: Estimating the world cancer burden: Globocan 2000
sentences.sentence_text: Incidence, the number of new cases occurring, can be expressed as the annual number of cases (the volume of new patients presenting for treatment) or as a rate per 100,000 persons per year.

sentences.title: Estimating the world cancer burden: Globocan 2000
sentences.sentence_text: Incidence data are produced by population-based cancer registries.13 Registries may cover national populations or, more often, certain regions.

sentences.title: Estimating the world cancer burden: Globocan 2000
sentences.sentence_text: In developing countries in particular, coverage is often confined to the capital city and its environs.

sentences.title: Estimating the world cancer burden: Globocan 2000
sentences.sentence_text: It was estimated that, in 1990, about 18% of the world population were covered by registries, 64% of developed countries and 5% of developing countries, although the situation is improving each year.

sentences.title: Estimating the world cancer burden: Globocan 2000
sentences.sentence_text: The most recent volume of "Cancer Incidence in Five Continents" (CI5) contains comparable incidence information from 150 registries in 50 countries, primarily over the period 1988–1992.14 Survival statistics are also produced by cancer registries by the follow-up of registered cancer cases.

sentences.title: Estimating the world cancer burden: Globocan 2000
sentences.sentence_text: Population-based figures are published by registries in many developed countries, for example, the SEER program covering 10% of the U.S. population15 and the EUROCARE II project, including 17 countries of Europe.16 Survival data from populations of China, the Philippines, Thailand, India and Cuba have been published by Sankaranarayanan et al.17 Mortality is the number of deaths occurring and the mortality rate the number of deaths per 100,000 persons per year.

sentences.title: Estimating the world cancer burden: Globocan 2000
sentences.sentence_text: It is the product of incidence and fatality (the inverse of survival) of a given cancer.

sentences.title: Estimating the world cancer burden: Globocan 2000
sentences.sentence_text: Mortality rates measure the average risk to the population of dying from a specific cancer, while fatality (1-survival) represents the probability that an individual with cancer will die from it.

sentences.title: Estimating the world cancer burden: Globocan 2000
sentences.sentence_text: Mortality data are derived from vital registration systems, where the fact and "underlying" cause of death are certified, usually by a medical practitioner.

sentences.title: Estimating the world cancer burden: Globocan 2000
sentences.sentence_text: Their great advantage is comprehensive coverage and availability.

sentences.title: Estimating the world cancer burden: Globocan 2000
sentences.sentence_text: By 1990, about 42% of the world population was covered by vital registration systems producing mortality statistics on cancer.

sentences.title: Estimating the world cancer burden: Globocan 2000
sentences.sentence_text: Not all are, however, of the same quality in all countries.

sentences.title: Estimating the world cancer burden: Globocan 2000
sentences.sentence_text: National-level statistics are collated and made available by the World Health Organiztion (http://www-dep.iarc.fr/dataava/globocan/who.htm), although for some countries coverage of the population is manifestly incomplete (so that the so-called mortality rates produced are implausibly low) and in others, quality of cause of death information is poor.

sentences.title: Estimating the world cancer burden: Globocan 2000
sentences.sentence_text: Frequency data, e.g., case series from hospitals and pathology laboratories, provide an indication of the relative importance of different cancers in a country or region in the absence of a population-based registry and mortality statistics.

sentences.title: Estimating the world cancer burden: Globocan 2000
sentences.sentence_text: There are problems in extrapolating the results to the general population, since such series are subject to various forms of selection bias.

sentences.title: Estimating the world cancer burden: Globocan 2000
sentences.sentence_text: Such data are generally published locally or in journal articles, although a few compendia are available.18, 19 Prevalence is the proportion of a population that has the disease at a given point in time.20 For many diseases (e.g., hypertension, diabetes), prevalence usefully describes the number of individuals requiring care.

sentences.title: Estimating the world cancer burden: Globocan 2000
sentences.sentence_text: For cancer, however, many persons diagnosed in the past have been "cured"—they no longer have an excess risk of death (although some residual disability may be present, for example, following a resective operation).

sentences.title: Estimating the world cancer burden: Globocan 2000
sentences.sentence_text: A straightforward comparison of need for cancer services can be made using partial prevalence, cases diagnosed within 1, 3 and 5 years, to indicate the numbers of persons undergoing initial treatment (cases within 1 year of diagnosis), clinical follow-up (within 3 years) or not considered "cured" (before 5 years).

sentences.title: Estimating the world cancer burden: Globocan 2000
sentences.sentence_text: Patients alive 5 years after diagnosis are usually considered cured since, for most cancers, the death rates of such patients are similar to those in the general population.

sentences.title: Estimating the world cancer burden: Globocan 2000
sentences.sentence_text: The methods used to produce the estimates are summarised in several recent articles.5, 6, 21, 22 The "Help" option of GLOBOCAN 2000 lists the sources of data and methods used for each country.

sentences.title: Estimating the world cancer burden: Globocan 2000
sentences.sentence_text: National incidence data from good-quality cancer registries.

sentences.title: Estimating the world cancer burden: Globocan 2000
sentences.sentence_text: National mortality data, with estimation of incidence using sets of regression models specific for site, sex and age, derived from local cancer registry data (incidence plus mortality).

sentences.title: Estimating the world cancer burden: Globocan 2000
sentences.sentence_text: Local (regional) incidence data from 1 or more regional cancer registries within a country.

sentences.title: Estimating the world cancer burden: Globocan 2000
sentences.sentence_text: When there are several cancer registries in the country, their incidence rates must be combined into a common set of values by some weighted average.

sentences.title: Estimating the world cancer burden: Globocan 2000
sentences.sentence_text: Local mortality data from some sort of sample survey of deaths, converted to incidence using specific models.

sentences.title: Estimating the world cancer burden: Globocan 2000
sentences.sentence_text: Frequency data.

sentences.title: Estimating the world cancer burden: Globocan 2000
sentences.sentence_text: For several developing countries, only data on the relative frequency of different cancers (by age and sex) are available.

sentences.title: Estimating the world cancer burden: Globocan 2000
sentences.sentence_text: These are applied to an estimated "all sites" incidence rate, derived from existing cancer registry results, in 7 world regions (Eastern Africa, Middle Africa, Northern Africa, Southern Africa, Western Africa, Middle East and Other Oceania).

sentences.title: Estimating the world cancer burden: Globocan 2000
sentences.sentence_text: No data.

sentences.title: Estimating the world cancer burden: Globocan 2000
sentences.sentence_text: The country-specific rates are those of the corresponding world area (calculated from the other countries for which estimates could be made).

sentences.title: Estimating the world cancer burden: Globocan 2000
sentences.sentence_text: There are few large countries that fall into this category.

sentences.title: Estimating the world cancer burden: Globocan 2000
sentences.sentence_text: Those with a population greater than 10 million were Morocco, Afghanistan, Nepal, Sri Lanka, Mozambique, Madagascar and Yemen.

sentences.title: Estimating the world cancer burden: Globocan 2000
sentences.sentence_text: National mortality rates, with for some countries a correction factor applied to account for known and quantified underreporting of deaths.

sentences.title: Estimating the world cancer burden: Globocan 2000
sentences.sentence_text: Rates for missing sites were computed using proportions from mortality files provided by cancer registries.

sentences.title: Estimating the world cancer burden: Globocan 2000
sentences.sentence_text: When no national mortality data are available, local (regional) mortality rates derived from the data of 1 or more cancer registries covering a part of a country (state, province, etc.)

sentences.title: Estimating the world cancer burden: Globocan 2000
sentences.sentence_text: were used.

sentences.title: Estimating the world cancer burden: Globocan 2000
sentences.sentence_text: When mortality data were unavailable or known to be of poor quality, mortality was estimated from incidence, using country/region-specific survival (see prevalence data).

sentences.title: Estimating the world cancer burden: Globocan 2000
sentences.sentence_text: In the absence of any data, country-specific rates are calculated from the average of those of neighbouring countries in the same regions.

sentences.title: Estimating the world cancer burden: Globocan 2000
sentences.sentence_text: Estimates of partial prevalence in each country were derived by combining the annual number of new cases and the corresponding probability of survival by time.

sentences.title: Estimating the world cancer burden: Globocan 2000
sentences.sentence_text: For example, 1-year prevalence at a fixed point in mid-2000 was estimated from the number of new cases in 2000 multiplied by the probability of surviving at least 6 months, and 3-year prevalence sums the numbers alive at 0.5, 1.5 and 2.5 years.

sentences.title: Estimating the world cancer burden: Globocan 2000
sentences.sentence_text: Relative survival data were obtained from the sources cited above and converted to observed survival using "normal" mortality probability (derived from the corresponding life tables).

sentences.title: Estimating the world cancer burden: Globocan 2000
sentences.sentence_text: The shape of the survival curve from 0 to 5 years postdiagnosis was assumed to follow a Weibull distribution.22 GLOBOCAN 2000 presents incidence, mortality and prevalence data for 5 broad age groups (0–14, 15–44, 45–54, 55–64 and 65 and over) and sex for all countries of the world for 24 different types of cancer.

sentences.title: Estimating the world cancer burden: Globocan 2000
sentences.sentence_text: Since cancer data are collected and compiled sometime after the events to which they relate, the most recent statistics available are from periods from 3–10 years earlier.

sentences.title: Estimating the world cancer burden: Globocan 2000
sentences.sentence_text: The actual number of cancer cases, deaths and prevalent cases are calculated by applying these rates to the estimated world population for 2000, obtained from the most recent projections prepared by the United Nations Population Division.23 On the CD-ROM are computer programs to analyse and present the cancer database.

sentences.title: Estimating the world cancer burden: Globocan 2000
sentences.sentence_text: The database itself may be downloaded from the Internet (http://www-dep.iarc.fr/globocan/globocan.htm).

sentences.title: Estimating the world cancer burden: Globocan 2000
sentences.sentence_text: This site contains the most recently available estimates of the incidence and mortality rates in different countries worldwide.

sentences.title: Estimating the world cancer burden: Globocan 2000
sentences.sentence_text: GLOBOCAN 2000 can present the statistics described at any level of geographical aggregation and in tabular or graphical format (maps, bar charts, age-specific curves and pie charts).

sentences.title: Estimating the world cancer burden: Globocan 2000
sentences.sentence_text: Some examples of these graphical presentations are shown on the cover of this issue.

sentences.title: Estimating the world cancer burden: Globocan 2000
sentences.sentence_text: Tabulations of numbers and rates may also be displayed and printed.

sentences.title: Estimating the world cancer burden: Globocan 2000
sentences.sentence_text: Incorporation of population projections for 5-year intervals, from 2005 to 2050,23 allows GLOBOCAN 2000 to be used to prepare projections of future burden, assuming current rates of incidence and mortality, or incorporating age/sex-specific rates of change in the rates.

sentences.title: Estimating the world cancer burden: Globocan 2000
sentences.sentence_text: Table I shows the most basic summary data of all—the global numbers of cases, deaths and prevalent cancers (within 5 years of diagnosis) by cancer site in males, females and both sexes.

sentences.title: Estimating the world cancer burden: Globocan 2000
sentences.sentence_text: There are an estimated 10.1 million new cases, 6.2 million deaths and 22.4 million persons living with cancer in the year 2000.

sentences.title: Estimating the world cancer burden: Globocan 2000
sentences.sentence_text: No attempt has been made to estimate incidence or mortality of nonmelanoma skin cancer because of the difficulties of measurement and consequent lack of data.

sentences.title: Estimating the world cancer burden: Globocan 2000
sentences.sentence_text: The total "All Cancer" therefore excludes such tumours.

sentences.title: Estimating the world cancer burden: Globocan 2000
sentences.sentence_text: The 2000 estimate represents an increase of around 22% in incidence and mortality since our most recent comprehensive estimates (for 1990).

sentences.title: Estimating the world cancer burden: Globocan 2000
sentences.sentence_text: Lung cancer is the main cancer in the world today, whether considered in terms of numbers of cases (1.2 million) or deaths (1.1 million), because of the high case fatality (ratio of mortality:incidence = 0.9).

sentences.title: Estimating the world cancer burden: Globocan 2000
sentences.sentence_text: However, breast cancer, although it is the second most common cancer overall (1.05 million new cases) ranks much less highly (5th) as a cause of death because of the relatively favourable prognosis (ratio of mortality:incidence = 0.4).

sentences.title: Estimating the world cancer burden: Globocan 2000
sentences.sentence_text: Colon plus rectum is third in importance in terms of new cases (945,000 cases, 492,000 deaths), and stomach cancer (876,000 cases, 647,000 deaths) fourth.

sentences.title: Estimating the world cancer burden: Globocan 2000
sentences.sentence_text: In terms of prevalence, the most common cancers are breast (3.9 million breast cancer cases), colorectal cancers (2.4 million) and prostate (1.6 million).

sentences.title: Estimating the world cancer burden: Globocan 2000
sentences.sentence_text: The ratio between prevalence and incidence is an indicator of prognosis.

sentences.title: Estimating the world cancer burden: Globocan 2000
sentences.sentence_text: This explains why breast cancer appears as the most prevalent cancer in the world, despite there being fewer new cases than for lung cancer, for which the outlook is considerably poorer.

sentences.title: Estimating the world cancer burden: Globocan 2000
sentences.sentence_text: Table II shows incidence rates for all cancers (excluding skin) by world area and sex.

sentences.title: Estimating the world cancer burden: Globocan 2000
sentences.sentence_text: Two indices are used, the age standardized rate per 100,000 (standardized to the world standard population) and the cumulative rate (percent), from birth to age 65.

sentences.title: Estimating the world cancer burden: Globocan 2000
sentences.sentence_text: Both of these indicators allow comparisons between populations that are not influenced by differences in their age structures.

sentences.title: Estimating the world cancer burden: Globocan 2000
sentences.sentence_text: Age standardized rates in developed countries are about twice those in developing countries; the differential is less for the cumulative rate, which ignores disease rates in the 65 and over age groups.

sentences.title: Estimating the world cancer burden: Globocan 2000
sentences.sentence_text: On average, worldwide, there is about a 10% chance of getting a cancer before age 65.

sentences.title: Estimating the world cancer burden: Globocan 2000
sentences.sentence_text: Incidence (and mortality) rates are highest in North America, Australia/New Zealand and Western Europe, and lowest in parts of Africa.

sentences.title: Estimating the world cancer burden: Globocan 2000
sentences.sentence_text: This overall risk is, of course, dependent upon the contributions of different types of cancer.

sentences.title: Estimating the world cancer burden: Globocan 2000
sentences.sentence_text: For example, in West Africa, incidence of almost all cancers is low (except for cervix cancer in women and liver cancer in men).

sentences.title: Estimating the world cancer burden: Globocan 2000
sentences.sentence_text: This contrasts with Southern Africa, which has, in addition, high rates of lung and oesophagus cancer, and with East Africa, with high rates of AIDS-related tumours, notably Kaposi's sarcoma.

sentences.title: Estimating the world cancer burden: Globocan 2000
sentences.sentence_text: The statistics used to assess the importance (burden) of cancer and of different types of cancer in the population either quantify the disease itself (the "need" for services) or the demand that it places upon them.24 Incidence rates provide a measure of the risk of developing specific cancers in different populations.

sentences.title: Estimating the world cancer burden: Globocan 2000
sentences.sentence_text: Changes in incidence are the appropriate indicator of the impact of primary prevention strategies.

sentences.title: Estimating the world cancer burden: Globocan 2000
sentences.sentence_text: Mortality rates are sometimes used as a convenient proxy measure of the risk of acquiring the disease (incidence) when comparing different groups, since they may be more generally available.

sentences.title: Estimating the world cancer burden: Globocan 2000
sentences.sentence_text: However, this use assumes equal survival in the populations being compared, and this assumption may well be incorrect, for example, there are well-documented differences between countries.

sentences.title: Estimating the world cancer burden: Globocan 2000
sentences.sentence_text: Mortality does provide an unambiguous measure of the outcome or impact of cancer and, used in conjunction with data on incidence, is the index of choice for the evaluation of the effects of early diagnosis or treatment.

sentences.title: Estimating the world cancer burden: Globocan 2000
sentences.sentence_text: Prevalence, as the number of persons ever diagnosed with cancer (lifetime prevalence), does not have much apparent utility.

sentences.title: Estimating the world cancer burden: Globocan 2000
sentences.sentence_text: The data can be derived from cancer registries that have very long-term registration of cases and complete follow-up for vital status over many years.25, 26 Population surveys are another approach, although they underestimate true prevalence.27 In the absence of complete data, an estimate can be prepared using models that incorporate longtime series of incidence and survival.28, 29 Other workers have attempted to define the proportion and timing of "cure" for different cancers, so that only patients not cured are considered prevalent.30 The data needed for such calculations are rarely available, however, and, for international comparisons, a simpler approach is needed.

sentences.title: Estimating the world cancer burden: Globocan 2000
sentences.sentence_text: Partial prevalence, as estimated in GLOBOCAN, as well as approximating the numbers of patients under treatment or follow-up, does not require long time series of incidence or survival data (or a further set of assumptions required to estimate them).

sentences.title: Estimating the world cancer burden: Globocan 2000
sentences.sentence_text: Compound indicators, which use information on the duration or severity of disease, have a genuine utility in setting priorities within health-care systems.

sentences.title: Estimating the world cancer burden: Globocan 2000
sentences.sentence_text: They include person-years of life lost (how many years of normal life span are lost due to deaths from cancer)31 and disability or quality-adjusted life-years lost.32, 33 The latter measures require that a numerical score is given to the years lived with a reduced quality of life between diagnosis and death (where quality = 0) or cure (quality = 1).

sentences.title: Estimating the world cancer burden: Globocan 2000
sentences.sentence_text: The problem with such indicators, however, is that there is simply insufficient quantitative information on quality or disability following a cancer diagnosis in different cultures (or countries) worldwide to permit calculation of valid comparative statistics.

sentences.title: Estimating the world cancer burden: Globocan 2000
sentences.sentence_text: The GLOBOCAN estimates of incidence, mortality and (5-year) prevalence help to define priorities for cancer control program (prevention and treatment, aided by early detection, if appropriate).

sentences.title: Estimating the world cancer burden: Globocan 2000
sentences.sentence_text: For countries with well-established sources of data, changes in the estimates over time indicate progress against cancer.

sentences.title: Estimating the world cancer burden: Globocan 2000
sentences.sentence_text: Incidence trends can monitor the success of prevention and the success of treatment (resulting from earlier diagnosis or more effective therapies).

sentences.title: Estimating the world cancer burden: Globocan 2000
sentences.sentence_text: In addition, the geographic patterns of cancer internationally serve one of the classic roles of descriptive epidemiology: observing whether the distribution of specific cancers follows the patterns expected from the distribution of known risk factors between populations or whether there are apparent anomalies that merit further investigation.
